Compiled code depends on a compiler contract . The core recognizes the contracts it supports; for code compiled with an unsupported contract, the consumer sees an MJX121 warning in development mode. Give the peerDependencies range according to the major version of the core you compiled the package with ( ^1.0.0 ); when the core's major version goes up, recompile and republish the package. noImplicitOverride : if your component classes accidentally shadow a member of ComponentBase ( dispose , controls , props , element …), you get a compile error. In a wrapper that does not use JSX the jsx lines are unnecessary. plugins: [compiler()] is still needed: it is what produces the element type from the generic in .ts files and transforms decorators. If you write the element yourself with static elementTag and use no decorators, you can drop it too; the rest is the same.

title: Publishing an npm Library for MotifJS
heading: Entry point and exports
text: Export the components and prop types by name ; a default export only makes sense for single components meant for Lazy /lazy route loading. You can offer heavy components (an editor, a chart, a map) from separate subpaths: exports["./editor"] + a build.lib.entry object. The consumer loads only what is needed with Lazy({ caller: () => import('@acme/motif-ui/editor') }) (see Lazy ).

title: Publishing an npm Library for MotifJS
heading: The prop contract
text: The package's components will be used in other people's code; define a prop surface that follows the compiler's rules: The consumer uses the component in their own form: In the function component, create is a local function inside the layout function. In a class, view() returns the content, not the root. The root element comes from the generic ( Component<HTMLButtonElement> ), from static elementTag or from a super("button") call; the root's class, attributes and events are attached in onConfigured . Writing a <button> again inside view() produces two nested elements. In Options, view() returns the content, not the root. The root element is the el field; the root's class, attributes and events are attached in onConfigured . Writing a <button> again inside view() produces two nested elements. In a function component the returned element is the root; classes, attributes and events are written directly on it. The rules: Every prop that can change is a Bind<T> and is read with read() . The consumer can write label="Save" or label={() => state.text} ; the compiler already wraps a ternary in an attribute in a getter (see Ternaries in attributes ). If the prop is read without read() , the getter form does not work. Common attributes fall through to the root. class , style , id , tabindex , role , aria-* and data-* are applied automatically from the component tag to the root element; do not define them as props and copy them by hand (see Attribute fallthrough ). The root's own class is merged with the consumer's. Do not use reserved names: options , ref , key , transition , childs , initializeComponent and the names of the lifecycle hooks ( onBuilt , onMounted …) go to the framework (see Careful with prop names ). Do not give a callback a name that clashes with a DOM event name. A prop such as onChange , onSelect , onResize , onReset , onCopy or onContextMenu on a component tag is attached to the root element as a DOM listener and never reaches the props; the compiler warns with MJX002 . Names such as onPress , onValueChange and onCommit are safe. Assume the consumer will reach the component instance through ref ; expose the behaviour you want to offer as a method ( dialog.open() ) and keep the inner fields closed. Child content arrives through childs ; in a class whose root element is declared with the generic or static elementTag and that writes no view() , the <Card>…</Card> form works directly. In a class that builds its root with super("div", props) , you place the children yourself (see Child components ). Child content arrives through props.childs and is placed inside the returned root (see Child components ). Child content arrives through childs ; in an Options component that writes no view() , the <Card>…</Card> form works directly, and the children are added to the el element. An Options component that writes view() places them itself with this.childs (see Child components ).

title: Publishing an npm Library for MotifJS
heading: Styles and CSS
text: Ship the package's CSS as a single file , and let the consumer import it deliberately: In library mode, CSS imported from src/index.ts is written as dist/style.css in Vite 5 (in Vite 6, give the name with build.lib.cssFileName: 'style' ); exports["./style.css"] makes it addressable. Importing it from the entry does not conflict with sideEffects: false : bundlers treat CSS files as having side effects. Put the rules inside an @layer ( @layer mf.base, mf.components; ). Unlayered rules override every layer regardless of specificity, so a one-line override by the consumer always wins; give theme values through prefixed CSS variables such as --mf-* . A <style> tag inside a component (see Inline style ) is useful for small, self-contained components, but it produces a <style> node in every instance and is not scoped; at library scale, prefer a file. Document the class names for transitions: a consumer who writes transition="mf-fade" expects the mf-fade-enter-from/active/to rules from you (see The transition prop ).

title: Publishing an npm Library for MotifJS
heading: Services
text: If the package carries a service (a theme, a notification queue, a language), mark it with @Injectable ; the class is marked the moment its module loads and is registered when the application is build() -ed. A class whose module loads after build() is registered on its first resolution (see Automatic registration with decorators ). The compiler plugin compiles decorators in .ts files too; in a wrapper without the plugin, TypeScript compiles the standard decorator itself. If the consumer needs to choose the lifetime, an explicit registration function is clearer: An explicit registration overrides the decorator, so giving both is safe.

title: Publishing an npm Library for MotifJS
heading: Testing and development
text: vitest + jsdom work with the same plugin as in vite.config.ts ; no extra setting is needed for JSX in tests. Add things to document and test the onMounted behaviour as well. Write a round-trip test for every component: build it, add it to the DOM, dispose() , and check that the number of live components went back to where it started (see Prove the cleanup ). A leak only shows up this way. For development, put an index.html and src/showcase/ in the package root, and look at the components in a real browser with vite . The showcase stays outside exports , so it does not go into the package. motif-lint (it comes with @motifx/compiler ) checks JSX against the prop types; add "lint:jsx": "motif-lint" to package.json (see motif-lint ).

title: Publishing an npm Library for MotifJS
heading: Pre-publish checks
text: npm run build → were dist/index.js , dist/index.cjs , dist/types/index.d.ts and dist/style.css created? Is there no jsx( / createElement( in dist/index.js , and is there a from "@motifx/core" ? (The compiler ran and the core stayed outside.) npx publint and npx @arethetypeswrong/cli --pack : are exports / types consistent, and does a CJS consumer see the types? Install the npm pack output in an empty Vite application and use a component; with app.useDevelopment(true) , check that no MJX121 or MJX002 warning appears. When testing in a monorepo linked with file: / link: , give resolve: { dedupe: ['@motifx/core'] } on the consumer side; the published package does not need this. In the README , write down the peer dependencies, the style.css import, the prop table and the transition class names.

title: Publishing an npm Library for MotifJS
heading: Next step
text: To inspect the component tree, reactivity and counters while developing a package, go on to The DevTools Contract .

title: The DevTools Contract
text: The core does not include a DevTools UI; it offers a single object that a UI can read and write. This page describes that object. It is for people writing a DevTools UI. A package author who wants to open their package's own state to DevTools reads the DevTools for Packages page; this page is the ground that one stands on.

title: The DevTools Contract
heading: Turning it on
text: DevTools is turned on only with app.useDevelopment(true) . This call turns on development mode as well. useDevelopment(false) turns both off. A parameter in the address bar or a global written by hand does not turn DevTools on. While it is on, globalThis.__MOTIF_DEVTOOLS__ holds the contract object; when it is turned off, the object is removed. While it is off, the core records nothing and produces no events. Counters and records are kept from the moment DevTools is turned on. Module-level stores ( export const cart = reactive({ … }) ) are created during import, that is, before the useDevelopment(true) call. When developing with the @motifx/compiler Vite plugin, every top-level const or let whose value comes from a reactive , useModel , createSignal , createComputed or createLazyComputed call of @motifx/core is named after its variable, in all .ts , .tsx , .js and .jsx files. These stores are listed in getStores() with a name ( cart ) and a file ( src/stores/cart.ts , relative to the Vite root). Nothing is added to a production build. Early stores held in a field of a component or a service enter the list through the scan done in the getStores() call; only stores held inside a closure and not named by the compiler stay invisible. version is the version of the contract, 2 today. It goes up when the meaning of a field changes; adding a new field does not change the version. coreVersion is the version of the @motifx/core package the application runs on ( '1.2.0' ).

title: The DevTools Contract
heading: Paths
text: Components have no id numbers. The tree is a forest: [] is the virtual Application node that holds all the roots, the first number of a path picks the root, and the rest are controls indices down from that root. The roots, in order, are the application shell that run() builds ( [0] ), the page layer app.layer ( Layer ) if it has been created, and the host component wrapping the body of every window opened or connected with app.windows ( Window ); the windows are in the order of app.windows.list . [0, 2] is the shell's third child, and [1, 0] is the layer's first child. The path of a component that is under no root is null . A path depends on the component's position in the list. When a component is added in front of it or the list is re-sorted, the path changes. That is why every addition, removal and move in the tree is reported with the tree:changed event; the event carries the current paths of the parent components that need to be read again. When the layer is created, or when a window opens or closes, the list of roots changes; that is reported in the same event with the path [] .

title: The DevTools Contract
heading: Events
text: on(fn) adds a listener and returns a function that removes it. Every event has the form { type, payload } . The payload of component events always contains { path, type, tag } ; for a component that is under no root, path is null . Event Payload tree:changed { parents } : the paths of the parent components that changed; [] when the list of roots changed. Changes in the same round arrive in a single event. documents:changed The list of documents connected to the application changed: {} . The list is read again with getDocuments() . component:built duration : the build time including children (ms). component:visibility visible ; only when the visibility changes. component:wait waiting ; only when the waiting state changes. component:disposing The component info. component:disposed duration ; path is the path at the moment the dispose started. reactivity:flush Once at the end of every reactivity round: { id, duration, runs, triggers, effects, operations } ; see Operations . operation:started A piece of work started (see Operations ): { id, kind, name?, data?, parent? } . operation:finished The work finished: { id, duration, error? } ; for async work, when the promise settles. stores:changed When a new store is registered, once per round however many stores are created: {} . The list is read again with getStores() . scopes:changed When a DI scope opens, is committed or closes, once per round: {} . The list is read again with getScopes() . service:created A service instance was created: { scope, token, lifetime, source, instance } . scope is the number in getScopes() , and source is class , factory or value ; a transient emits on every resolution. service:disposed A scope started closing one of its instances: { scope, token, lifetime, instance } . route:navigation-start { uri } . route:navigation-end { uri, requested, outcome, reason?, params, duration } ; every navigation closes with an outcome. warning { code, message, details } ; on every occurrence. error:caught { context, error } ; on every occurrence. extension:registered A package registered (see Packages ): { name } . extension:disposed Its registration was removed: { name } . extension:changed The package wants the UI to read it again: { name, source? } ; the panels if there is no source , that source if there is. extension:reveal The package wants the UI to show something: { name, target } ; target has the form { panel, route?, params?, state? } . ext:<name>:<type> An event emitted by a package (see Packages ). There is no event for the moment a component enters the page. Whether a component is on the page is read from the connected field in the tree.

title: The DevTools Contract
heading: Tree
text: getTree(path = [], depth = Infinity) : returns the component at the path and its subtree, down to the given depth, as plain data. Every node carries { path, type, tag, built, visible, waiting, disposed, connected, document, childCount, children? } . type is the class's name for a class component and the function's name for a function component. The [] node's type is Application and its tag is #roots ; the shell root is named Component , the layer Layer , and a window root Window , and the window root also carries the window's title as title . document is the position, in getDocuments() , of the document the element is in, the page being 0 ; a component whose element the application moves to another document itself keeps its place in the tree, and only document points to that document. A list ( {items.map(…)} in JSX, or bindings.list ) adds two fragments: List , which is the spot of the .map() expression among its siblings, and ListItems inside it, which is the range where the items sit; a component that builds its own list keeps its name and carries the ListItems . A condition appears under the name of the binding that builds it: Ternary ( bindings.ternary , a ? b : c in JSX), When ( bindings.when , a && b in JSX), Expression (a bindings.method that returns a component, {() => …} in JSX) or Switch ( bindings.switchCase ); as long as it shows nothing, an Empty sits inside it in place of what it shows. x-wait and x-display add nothing to the tree: the component keeps its name and appears as waiting. Nodes beyond the depth have no children , but they do have childCount . getElement(path) : the DOM node of the component at that path; for highlighting and scrolling. null for [] . pathOfElement(node) : climbs up from a DOM node and returns the path of the first component, whatever document the node is in; null if it is under no root. getDocuments() : the page's document and the documents connected to the application ( app.windows windows, those connected with connectDocument ), in the order the document field counts. tag is the element's tag name; #fragment for a fragment and #text for text.

title: The DevTools Contract
heading: Component contents
text: inspect(path) returns the inside of a single component as plain data. No internal object is created on the component while reading, and no user code is called. Field Content props A preview of every prop. A function is shown as { kind: 'function', name } and is not called. An array is { kind: 'array', length } , an object { kind: 'object', type, keys } , a component { kind: 'component', path, type } , a DOM node { kind: 'node', tag } , and a signal or computed { kind: 'signal', type: 'signal' \| 'computed', value, stale? } with a preview of its value; stale: true marks a computed that has not calculated its current value yet, and its getter is not run. fields The component's own fields (for example the class field state = reactive(…) ), in the same preview form as props ; the internal fields the framework writes on every component are not listed. A field that is a getter appears as { kind: 'getter' } and is not called. functionProps Only on the root of a function component: the props given to the function, in the same preview form as props . bindings { kind, property?, member?, updateMode?, active } ; kind : property , list , conditional , class , attr , style . events { name, type, dom, handler, modifiers } ; dom: false is a component event. hooks { name, method, handlers } : whether it is defined as a class method, and how many handlers are attached. classes { static, reactive: [{ id, classes }] } ; the current class set of the reactive sources. attributes { name, value, reactive } . services { scope, requested } : the services the component asked for with getService , and its DI scope. effects See Reactivity trace . extensions The output of the packages that provide data for this component. window Only on a window root: { kind, title, open, components } ; kind is popup , pip or attached , and components is the number of components in the window. readValue(path, source, keys) opens one level of a value inside props , functionProps or fields ( source ): keys is the path to the value ( ['stat', 'tags'] ). The result is { ok: true, value: { value, entries: [{ key, value, getter? }], total } } in the same preview form; at most 100 fields are returned, and total gives the full count. Getters and functions are never called: a getter appears as getter: true , and a path that goes through a getter returns { ok: false, error: 'getter' } . Arrays, plain objects, class instances, Map (with keys as text) and Set (by position) can be opened; a path that goes through a signal or a computed continues into its value. readStore(id, keys) opens the inside of a store in getStores() the same way; for signals and computeds, the inside of the value is opened. getServices() lists the services registered in the application as { token, lifetime, created } . getScopes() lists the DI scopes and the services created in each: Field Content id , parent The scope's number and the number of its parent scope; parent is null at the root. kind , name root , navigation (one per navigation) or user (opened with createScope(name) ), and the scope's name. current The scope from which the current page gets its scoped services. pending A navigation scope that is still being built and has not been committed. pins The number of components outside the current page that still hold the scope, for example a page kept with keepAlive or a leaving page whose disposal is in progress. A previous navigation scope lives while this number is above zero. services { token, lifetime, instance, creating? } : singletons at the root and scoped services in every scope, in the same preview form as props ; creating: true while an async service is being built. transients The transient instances the scope holds in order to close them, while enableAutoDisposeTransients() is on. A scope opened with createScope is listed for as long as it is used, and leaves the list with dispose() . The scopes:changed event says when to read the list again. readService(scope, token, keys) opens one level of a service instance in the same form as readValue : scope is the number in getScopes() , and token is the name shown in that scope's services list. Singletons are read from the root scope, and scoped services from the scope that created them. Reading never creates the service: a service that has not been created yet returns { ok: false, error: 'no service' } . Only the instance's own fields are listed; getters on the class and #private fields are not.

title: The DevTools Contract
heading: Reactivity trace
text: inspect(path).effects lists the effects the component owns. A record looks like this: kind tells where the effect comes from: binding:<property> , list , when , method , ternary , watch , switch , conditional , class , attr:<name> , style , virtual-data , computed . Those created directly with effect() appear as effect and have no owner. The reactivity:flush event arrives once per round. triggers carries the changes that started that round, with their counts, and effects carries the effects that ran, with the paths of their owning components. If the changed object belongs to a store in getStores() , the trigger also carries a store: { id, path } field: path is the keys from the store's root to the changed object (a change to stats[1].value arrives as { path: ['stats', '1'] } and key: 'value' ). For signals and computeds the key is value . A thousand changes to the same value in one round are still a single event. Every flush has an increasing id . A trigger that happens inside an operation carries an operationId ; operations lists the ids of the operations the triggers of that round belong to. Changes to the same value in different operations are counted separately.

title: The DevTools Contract
heading: Counters
text: getCounters() returns, in a single call, an object that carries these fields: Field Meaning components.live The number of live components components.inTree The number of components in the application tree components.notInTree The number of components that are alive but not in the tree components.byType The live count per component type ( { NoteRow: 12 } ) bindings The number of bindings in the tree listeners.dom / listeners.component DOM listeners / component event listeners effects.live / effects.owned Live effects / those of them owned by a component reactivity.runs The number of effect runs reactivity.flushes / reactivity.flushRuns The number of rounds / the total effects run in rounds reactivity.lastFlushDuration / reactivity.maxFlushDuration The duration of the last round / of the longest round (ms) All the fields are numbers; byType is an object from type name to number. live goes up when a component is built and down when it is disposed. inTree , bindings and listeners are counted by walking the tree at the time of the call. notInTree is the components that are alive but not in the tree; if it does not drop even after leaving the page, those components are being held somewhere. The counters start from zero every time DevTools is turned on.

title: The DevTools Contract
heading: Router, errors and warnings
text: getRoute() : the current { uri, params, chain } . getNavigations() : the last 50 navigations, { requested, uri, outcome, reason?, params, duration, at } . outcome : done , skipped , cancelled ( reason : middleware , onLeave , guard or the reason given by onLeave ), notFound , error . When a guard redirects to another address, two records are created: first the redirected navigation, then the outer navigation that keeps the requested address and the reached address apart. getRoutes() : the defined routes. getWarnings() : warnings are merged by code and message: { code, message, details, count, firstAt, lastAt } . At most 200 records are kept; when full, the one not seen for the longest time is deleted. details stays as it was on the first occurrence. getErrors() : errors are merged the same way, by context, name and message; at most 100 records. getStores() : the reactive , useModel , signal and computed records created while devtools is on and still in use; stores held in a field of a component or a service that were created before devtools was turned on are also taken into the list during the scan. Each record is { id, name, file?, type, value, stale?, released?, holders } ; the name and file fields of a module store come from the compiler (see above). holders lists the components ( { kind: 'component', path, type, field } ) and services ( { kind: 'service', token, lifetime, field } ; field: null if the service itself is the store) that hold the store in one of their fields; the list is worked out on every call by scanning the component tree and the created services, without calling getters. An empty list means the store is held at module level or inside a closure. A store that used to be held in a field of a component or a service and no longer is comes with released: true (for example the state field of a component that has closed). An unused store drops out of the list when the garbage collector collects it; the browser decides when that happens. The value of a signal or a computed is its current value; a computed's getter is not run while reading it, and a computed that has never been calculated or is stale comes with stale: true .

title: The DevTools Contract
heading: Write operations
text: Every write goes through the public API that application code uses too. The result is { ok: true, value? } or { ok: false, error } ; the operations do not throw. Operation What it does setClass(path, name, on) class.add / class.remove . setAttribute(path, name, value) attr.add ; value: null deletes. Names starting with on… are not written. setVisible(path, visible) motif.show() / motif.hide() ; transitions are awaited. Roots are not hidden: a single-number path returns ok: false . writeModel(path, value) bindings.writeModel(value) ; ok: false if there is no model binding. setProp(path, keys, value) Writes to the key path on props , then runs the bindings again with setState() . navigate(uri) router.navigate(uri) . setStoreValue(id, keys, value) Writes to a reactive or signal record by its id in getStores() ; for a signal with empty keys , it replaces the value itself. A computed cannot be written. Reactivity works as usual. callExtension(name, panel, command, args) Runs a command a package registered (see Packages ); only from a panel whose capabilities grant write permission. The command's return value is awaited and becomes value . The keys __proto__ , prototype and constructor are not written.

title: The DevTools Contract
heading: Next step
text: A package that shows its own state in DevTools registers with registerDevtools : DevTools for Packages . For a summary of every exported symbol, go on to API Reference .

title: DevTools for Packages
text: A package (a component library, a data layer, a store) can show its own state in DevTools without depending on a DevTools UI: it registers with the core, and the UI reads what it provides. This page covers the core side: what registerDevtools takes, what its handle does, and how a package says which piece of work changed what. The object the UI reads is on The DevTools Contract page. What the @motifx-community/devtools panel draws from panel metadata, its widgets, routes and limits are described in that package's docs/extensions.md file, not here.

title: DevTools for Packages
heading: registerDevtools for packages
text: A package opens its own state from the @motifx/core/devtools subpath. describe and inspect provide data; with sources , commands and panels the UI reads when it wants to, sends commands to the page and knows what to draw. In the example, the folder chart from the Wrapping Third-Party Libraries page keeps the charts it builds by component and gives their data to DevTools: Registration can happen at any time; a package can register the moment it is imported. describe , inspect , sources , commands and panels given as a function are called only when the UI asks. The result of describe() is read with readExtension(name) , and the result of inspect(component) inside inspect(path).extensions[name] . A package that returns undefined is not listed for that component. The result of a function that throws becomes { error } ( describe , inspect ) or { ok: false, error } (sources, commands, panels ); the other data is not affected. panels says what the UI will draw for this package: id , title , icon , order , capabilities , and whatever else the UI's own schema defines ( layout , routes ). The core stores it as it is and reads only id and capabilities . If it is given as a function, it is called on every read. readExtensionPanels(name) returns { panels, sources, commands } : the panels, the settings of each source other than its read ( key , events , max ), and the command names. sources are named functions the UI reads with parameters. readExtensionSource(name, panel, source, params) awaits read(params) and returns { ok: true, value } . key names the field that identifies a row, events maps the package's own event types to what the UI will do with them ( upsert , append , remove , refresh ), and max limits the number of rows the UI keeps; the core carries these three to the UI and does not use them itself. commands are named functions the UI runs with callExtension . A command can return a promise. capabilities is read per panel on every read and call: read allows readExtensionSource , write allows callExtension , and subscribe lets the package's events through. A field that is not written is false . Denials have the form { ok: false, error } and carry not allowed , no extension , no source or no command . Only own keys exist in sources and commands ; constructor and __proto__ are not there. emit(type, payload) emits the event under the name ext:<name>:<type> ; it does nothing while DevTools is off, nor when the registration has panels and none of them has subscribe . A registration without panels emits as before. changed(source?) emits extension:changed so that the UI reads the panels (without an argument) or that source again; reveal(target) emits extension:reveal with { panel, route?, params?, state? } . Both do so only while DevTools is on and while the registration is the current registration for its name. pathOf(component) gives the component's DevTools path. dispose() removes the registration and emits extension:disposed . A new registration under the same name replaces the old one; the old registration's dispose() does not delete the new one. A registration made while DevTools is on emits extension:registered . getExtensions() lists the names of the registered packages. Everything the core does not read (the shape of a panel apart from id and capabilities , the meaning of key , events and max , the content of a reveal target) is a contract between the UI and the package; the core carries it as it is.

title: DevTools for Packages
heading: Operations and write records
text: @motifx/core/devtools also exports what a package needs to say which piece of work changed what : operations and write records. They are for packages that keep history, draw a timeline or explain a change; application code has no need for them. An operation is the work running at the moment: a click handler, a navigation, a package's action. It is a single value the core holds while a function is running, just as it holds the running effect. It is not tied to the application or the component tree, it is not passed down, and components do not see it. Writes, flush triggers and operation events carry its id . startOperation(info) gives { id, kind, name?, data?, parent? } . The core provides the id (an increasing number) and the parent (the operation running at that moment); no other field is copied from info . kind is any text the package chooses. resumeOperation(operation, fn) makes it the current operation while fn runs and puts the previous one back; null runs fn outside any operation. It can be called as many times as needed. endOperation(operation, error?) ends it once; later calls do nothing. Resuming an operation that has ended still records under it, and warns once in development ( MJX211 ). runOperation(info, fn) is the three in a single call. If fn returns a promise, the operation ends when the promise settles, and runOperation returns a promise that follows it: the same value, the same rejection. While DevTools is off, it returns the result of fn as it is. JavaScript carries no value across an await ; after an await there is no current operation, and the code above brings it back with resumeOperation . Do not rely on what currentOperation() gives after an await . operation:started carries the operation, and operation:finished carries { id, duration, error? } ; both only while DevTools is on. startOperation , resumeOperation and endOperation stay in production too; their cost is an assignment. onWrite(fn) reports every reactive write while DevTools is on, and returns a function that stops it. Every record has a target (the raw object, array, Map , Set or signal) and, if it happened inside an operation, an operationId : kind When Fields add a new key on an object, an index past the end of an array, a new key in a Map or a new value in a Set key , value update a changed value: an object key, an array index, a growing length , a Map value, signal.value ( key: 'value' ) key , previous , value delete delete obj.key , map.delete(k) , set.delete(v) key , previous clear map.clear() , set.clear() removed : the map's [key, value] pairs, the set's values splice push , pop , shift , unshift , splice , sort , reverse , a shrinking length method , index , removed , added mutate signal.mutate(fn) ; the core cannot see what fn changed – Values arrive as they are stored: references, not copies. A listener that wants a snapshot takes it itself. A write that changes nothing (the same value again, a sort that keeps the order) is not reported. An array method is a single record; the index writes it makes inside are not reported. items.length = 1 reports the cut-off items as a splice with method: 'length' . Several listeners can be registered; one that throws is skipped. The writes a listener makes itself are not reported, so a listener can keep its records in reactive state. The records are for development. Every report in the core is a @DEV-ONLY statement, and a production build removes them; when used without the compiler, each one is a single check that is false while DevTools is off. A production history of what the application does belongs to the application itself: a service method and its inverse.

title: DevTools for Packages
heading: Next step
text: For a summary of every exported symbol, go on to API Reference .

title: Writing a Component Library
text: A component library (controls, a data grid, a scheduler) is used in applications it does not know, and often with thousands of its parts on a single page. Application code can lean on reactivity; library code should not. The rules on this page were worked out by writing a complete kit and measuring it. Read the Creating Components and bindings pages first.

title: Writing a Component Library
heading: Three ways in
text: A library component listens to only three things: Its props: each one a value or a function ( Bind<T> ). The developer's data: used as it is. The same objects are kept and handed back; they are not wrapped with reactive() , copied or transformed. A change made in place is read again with reState() or an explicit refresh() . The developer's reState() call. Everything else is the component's own state, and the component draws it by hand.

title: Writing a Component Library
heading: Props: a value or a function, tracked by a single binding
text: Every prop and every property setter takes a value or a function. A function is tracked by a single binding of the component. This binding is registered with bindings.add(binding) (the IBaseBinding shape; see Binding a component property ). Since it is in the component's binding registry, the developer's reState() call reaches it; plain data works as well as reactive data. The value is passed on if it differs from the last one read ( Object.is ). A reState() that finds the same value does not spoil what the user did in the meantime (the text they typed, the day they moved to). A property assigned from code stops tracking its function. To draw a property, a list of appliers is used, not an effect: the value is applied now and on every change, without tracking. No effect is created at all for a property given as a plain value. Data objects whose fields can be functions (menu items, toolbar items, summary items): all the fields of a source are read by a single binding, the values read are stored, and drawing is done from them. The developer's function is not called again while drawing; a function that returns a new node would produce a new node on every draw. A value that the user changes too (a text box, a list, a checkbox) is given to the control only when its source changes, not on every draw; otherwise what the user typed gets overwritten:

title: Writing a Component Library
heading: Nothing is tracked inside
text: A change is announced where it is made. Every piece of the component's state calls tell(name) . The names are collected and announced once per round; every view redraws the parts that the announced names concern. Nothing watches the state. The component's response to a change runs before the views. Reloading, re-laying out and closing an editor run first; what they announce joins the same round, and the views draw once. Such a response runs when the values it reads differ from the ones it read last. Stable values are compared: objects and Map s rebuilt on every read never come out equal, so they are keyed as JSON. Counters, such as a "read again" counter, go into the key too. Only a real change is announced. A notification announced on every draw is a loop (draw, announce, draw) and can lock up a browser tab. Parts drawn by hand are components built in code. JSX is not used there: the compiler turns every expression that reads a variable, even an attribute, into a binding. There is no bindings.watch or free effect() either. On a data grid page: bindings went down from 1,306 to 87; effects running at startup went down from 2,478 to 346; a sort now runs no effects at all (140 before). Reactive state can stay for the application. An API documented as "reactive" (a total, the number of selected rows) can keep its store for the application's own bindings; the component never reads it with tracking. A language or locale change is an event , not a signal. Every control subscribes once and draws its texts and formats now and on every change; the subscription goes away with the control: Content that does not change is built once. {cond && <X/>} and .map rows given a key open bindings per item. Content that does not change can be built once with controls.add inside onConfig or initializeComponent . On a documentation page, this brought the page's effect count down from 16 thousand to 10 thousand.

title: Writing a Component Library
heading: The component's tree
text: view() returns a single ComponentBase . Several parts are put inside motifFragment() ; <>…</> compiles to this too. Parts that have to be direct children of the element (header cells, moved rows) are not returned from view() ; they are added inside initializeComponent (an override). Keyed parts are matched by hand. A node that is already in place is never moved: moving the focused element takes away its focus. controls.remove(part) takes the part out right away. part.dispose() removes its element one round later; a draw made right after that still finds the element. A part that is shown and hidden in place, like x-display , swaps places with a comment placeholder and is put back there. The placeholder needs a parent, which is why the top-level parts are drawn for the first time inside onBuilt .

title: Writing a Component Library
heading: Writing only on change
text: Rewriting an attribute, a style or a text even with the same value makes the browser recalculate styles. Hand-drawing code that rewrote unchanged attributes on every draw did five times the style calculation of the reactive code it replaced. A value is written only when it changes. Replacing a constructable stylesheet ( replaceSync ) with the same text invalidates the styles of the whole document. A grid that rewrote the column stylesheet on every step while a column was being widened spent 60–110 ms per step. When the sheet was written only when its text changed, the long tasks went away.

title: Writing a Component Library
heading: Lifetime
text: Disposing a component sets its own fields to undefined . Callbacks that arrive later (timers, promises, observers, a deferred draw) check isDisposed first. onDisposing runs before the element leaves the DOM, and removing a focused element triggers focusout . So a focusout handler can run on a component that is being disposed. If focus has to move away from a control that is being hidden or deactivated, the next control is focused with focus({ preventScroll: true }) ; otherwise the page scrolls to it. ref callbacks run inside the base constructor, before the subclass's field initializers. State a ref may touch is kept not in class fields but in a symbol-keyed object created when needed.

title: Writing a Component Library
heading: Long work
text: Promise.then and queueMicrotask do not let the browser paint; a chain of microtasks is still a single long task. Long work is split into pieces with macrotasks ( setTimeout , MessageChannel ). Measured: with microtasks, a single 300 ms long task; with setTimeout pieces, no long task at all, and 18 painted frames.

title: Writing a Component Library
heading: Checking the work
text: Bindings are counted per component type by walking the component tree ( DevTools inspect(path).bindings ); counting only live effects is not enough. A binding that tracks a prop has no effect owner and does not show up in the effect count. While a view is being rewritten, the old and the new version are compared pixel by pixel on every page of that view. At every step the tests and e2e checks are kept green, and the drop in the effect count is proven. An e2e check that reads the page right after load waits for the content first: pages draw their sections after load .

title: Writing a Component Library
heading: Next step
text: To publish the library, go on to the Publishing an npm Library for MotifJS page.

title: API Reference
text: This section is a quick reference of the main symbols exported from the @motifx/core package. Every row links to the related detailed section.

title: API Reference
heading: Application
text: Symbol Kind Description Application class The application instance. The global instance is reached through Application.main , and from a component through context ( this.context in a class and in Options, the context of the root component in a function component). Application.CreateBuilder() static Produces an ApplicationBuilder . ApplicationBuilder class Carries the services collection; produces an Application with build() . app.run(host, root?) method Mounts the application on a DOM element. If host is a comment or text node, the application is placed right in front of that node and the node stays in place; if the node has no parent element, MJX416 is thrown. A disposed application starts again with run() : Application.main is filled again, services are created again on first request (those with startup: true right away), a new module is set up with the router configuration, the useTransitions mode is applied again, a layer read in the meantime is moved after the host, and dispose() works again. If a new application was set up in the meantime, MJX405 is thrown. app.useRouter(opts) method Defines routing. app.restartRouter(uri?) method Sets up the router from scratch and restarts it from the root ( / ) or from the given address: if a new useRouter configuration was given while running, it uses that, otherwise the current configuration. The route list, the keepAlive cache and the stack are reset; the page on screen leaves like a leaving page and the new page is built ( onRouterChanged runs with initial: true ); the address is written over the current history entry. Returns the result of the startup navigation. Has no effect before run . app.connectDocument(doc) method Connects another document of the same origin (a window.open window or an <iframe> ) to the application: the router's link catcher and the stack's scroll listeners are set up on that document too. It is counted; the function it returns undoes the connection, which also comes undone on its own when the document's window gets pagehide , and app.dispose() undoes all of them. It has no effect for the page's own document. A value that is not a document, has no window or cannot be accessed throws MJX417 . app.windows property The window manager ( WindowManager ): open(component, options) opens the component in a new window, or always on top with kind: "pip" , and returns an AppWindow handle; create , attach , of , supports , closeAll ; list is reactive; the events are window-opened / window-closed . See: Windows . app.layer property The page layer ( Component ): the first time it is read, it puts a plain <div> at the end of <body> , after the host element, and returns the component that wraps it (if the host is <body> itself or contains the layer, the layer stays at the end of the host and the shell content goes in front of it); it writes no styles or attributes, can be read before run() too (if there is no <body> yet, it is placed when the document loads; if the element has been taken out of the page, it is put back at the end of the body the first time content asks for a place, or in run() ), and app.dispose() disposes it together with its contents and removes the element. See: Page layer . app.layerOf(target?, ...components) method Returns the layer of the target's (a component or a DOM node) document: the host if it is an app.windows window, otherwise, or if there is no target, app.layer ; it adds the given components there with controls.add . A first component that has no parent and whose element is in no document is content, not a target; a root without a parent whose element sits in a document is a target. A target that is neither a component nor a node throws MJX424 . app.navigate(uri, options?) / app.navigateByName(name, params?, options?) method Navigation in code; the options are passed on to the router ( NavigationOptions ). Returns the result of the navigation (e.g. { ok: false, cancelled: true, reason: 'guard' } when a guard cancels it). app.router.navigate(uri, options?) method Navigation with options: { replace?, state?, force?, scroll? } ( NavigationOptions ). app.router property A single object for the whole application ( Router ); reactive, read-only route fields: params , route , uri , ok , meta , extend , fullPath , aliasOf , chain , direction , state , stack (only while stack is on). See: Navigation and Route State . app.useGuard(guard) / app.use(mw) method A navigation guard / middleware. For after a navigation, app.onRouterChanged(fn) . app.on/fire/off method The application event bus. on returns an unsubscribe function. app.onRouterChanged(fn) method Runs on every navigation (startup and 404 included) with { uri, params, meta, route, ok, initial, redirectedFrom?, direction, state } . app.onLifecycle(fn) method The application lifecycle: { state, visible, online } ; state : 'visible' \| 'hidden' \| 'frozen' \| 'resumed' \| 'restored' \| 'online' \| 'offline' . Returns an unsubscribe function. See: Lifecycle . app.isVisible / app.isOnline property The current visibility and connectivity state. app.router.evict(name \| route?) method Disposes the instances in the keepAlive cache (with no argument: all of them). app.router.resolve(uri) / app.router.href(name, params?) / app.router.routes method / property Matching without navigating ( RouteResolution : { chain, result } ), the path of a named route, and the route list in definition order ( RouteInfo[] ). See: The Route Table . app.router.scrollPositions() / app.router.restoreScrollPositions(positions) / app.router.saveScrollPositions(fn) method The scroll memory's positions ( { "/notes": 1200 } , including that of the page on screen); adds the given positions to the memory (before run() too); calls fn(positions) every time saving is needed (when leaving a page, on pagehide , when the page is hidden, on app.dispose() ) and returns a function that removes the subscription. Empty / no effect while scrollMemory is off. See: Scroll memory . app.useDevelopment(b) / app.useLogging(b) / app.useReactiveMonitor(o) method Development configuration. app.dispose() method → Promise<void> Sets app.state to 'disposing' ; disposes the router and the lifecycle listeners, and rolls back the address according to the router's mode ( history : / ; hash / file : only # is removed; shell and no router: not touched) (these happen synchronously). Then it disposes the route pages (with their leave animations) and the shell that run() set up (its RouterView and the root given to run() included), disposes the service provider last, and empties Application.main . While the tree is torn down, every component and the code running during animations see the same services and context . The host element stays on the page, empty. The promise resolves when everything, the services' async dispose s included, is finished: await app.dispose() ; a second call in the same life returns the same promise; in an application restarted with run() , dispose() works again; called again on a finished application, it disposes the layer, windows, document connections and recreated services set up since then, and does not touch the address or the transition mode; a call that arrives while this is in progress gets the same promise too. app.state property → ApplicationState 'initializing' (set up), 'running' ( run() was called), 'disposing' ( dispose() is in progress), 'disposed' (can be restarted with run() ). While an application is 'disposing' , a new Application.CreateBuilder() can be set up; the pages being torn down keep seeing their own application's services. useApplication() fn { application, services, router, windows, layer, layerOf, attach } . useNavigation() fn The same object as app.router ( Router ). See: Getting Started , Introduction to Routing .

title: API Reference
heading: Components
text: Symbol Kind Description Component class The concrete component class. super('div') or super() . ComponentBase class The base of all components. ComponentMotif class The type of the ComponentBase.motif namespace; the user does not create it with new . FNComponent(view) fn Wraps a function view in a component. motifComponent(el, props?) / motifFragment(props?) / motifCompiled(contract) / motifReport(error) fn The calls in the code the compiler produces ( _mc , _mf , _mv , _mr ); motifCompiled prints an MJX121 warning in development mode if the compiler contract does not match; motifReport reports, as MJX208 , an error caught in an expression the compiler wrapped in try / catch (a member call in child position, the left side of ?? / || , the condition of && ), and the expression's return value does not change. motifOptions(object) fn Returns the Options object as it is; on the type side it makes this in the methods the component ( ComponentBase & object ): this.class , this.motif and this.props compile in strict mode and the editor completes them. Its type is MotifOptions<T> ; the el key is required ( undefined / null is a fragment). Frame class A fragment container that holds/swaps a single piece of dynamic content: navigate(page, keepOldControl?) disposes the previous content and places the new one (it takes an array too), navigateLazy(() => import(...), options?) loads with Lazy , flush() disposes the content, current is the content shown, and isBusy tells whether a navigation is in progress. {() => expression} children and when / ternary / switchCase branches are built on top of it. See: Frame . ContentBody / ContentBlock class A multi-part body: <ContentBody name="x"/> is the body and <ContentBlock target="x">…</ContentBlock> is a part; several blocks pile up in the same body, and when a block is disposed it removes only its own parts. See: ContentBody and ContentBlock . Transport / TransportTo class Showing a component's content in a named slot outside its tree (e.g. moving page commands into the layout header). See: Transport and TransportTo . Transporter class Moving in code: Transporter.transport(child, newParent, { index?, keepState?, owner? }) , transportMany(children, newParent, options?) . See: Transport and TransportTo . FragmentNode class A component rooted in a fragment (a comment node); motifFragment() and <>…</> produce this. childs and props.nodes are added to the content. ControlCollection class The type of component.controls ; not created with new . Lazy({ caller, options? }) fn Lazy content through a dynamic import ( <Lazy caller={() => import('./X')} /> ; LazyOptions : Loaderview , Placeholderview , Fallbackview , minDelayMs , timeoutMs , signal , onError , mapResult , retry , onRetry ). See: Lazy . Virtualization<T> class A virtually scrolled list.

title: API Reference
heading: Main members of ComponentBase
text: Member Description element The real DOM node. props The component's props. controls The child control collection ( add(...c) / add(index, ...c) / insert(index, ...c) / remove / clear / clearAsync / detach / silentDetach / silentUnlink / move / moveToIndex / forEach / map / items / length ). See: Components . context The running Application ; the on / onRouterChanged subscriptions opened through it go away when the component is disposed. class / attr The class and attribute helpers. bindings The binding collection. state (user-defined) Usually reactive({...}) . view() The method that returns the component's content; not the root (the root element is declared on the class). motif The namespace of framework operations ( ComponentMotif ). A subclass can define names such as show , on , clear and options for its own purposes; the framework only uses the this.motif.* path. motif.on/off/trigger/addHandler Event handling; names with the x: prefix are lifecycle events ( x:built , x:mounted , x:disposed …). motif.show/hide/toggle Visibility. motif.options The component's settings object ( transition , hideStrategy , disableDisposal , chunk ). motif.stopAnimations() Finishes a running CSS class transition and cancels WAAPI animations. isWait Waiting (the counterpart of x-wait ; writable). isBuilt / isInitialized / isConfigured / isVisible / isDisposed State flags. parent / childs The parent component / the JSX children written between the tags. using(promise, onfulfilled?, onrejected?) / doWork(promise) Safe handling of async results after disposal. See: using , doWork . dispose/disposeAsync Disposal. motif.clear() Disposes the content (the children). motif.register/setDisposable Registering resources. getService(token) DI resolution. useModel(model) Produces a reactive model. style(...) / setText(...) Helpers. siblings all/next/prev/nextAll/prevAll . $(selector) fromDom() / fromComponent() queries.

title: API Reference
heading: Lifecycle hooks
text: onInitializing , onInitialized , onConfig , onConfigured , onBuilding , initializeComponent , oninitializeComponent , onBuilt , onMounted , onVisibilityChanged , onActivated , onDeactivated , onDisposing , onDisposed . onRefCreated(sender) : called after each ref={this.x} / ref={name} in the class's view() has been applied ( sender is the component that got the ref); not called for a ref in the callback form. See: Components . See: Components , Lifecycle .

title: API Reference
heading: Reactivity (store)
text: Symbol Signature Description reactive(model) <T>(m: T) => T A reactive proxy. useModel(model) <T>(m: T) => T An alias of reactive . createSignal(v) <T>(v: T) => Signal<T> A single-value signal. createComputed(fn) <T>(fn) => Computed<T> A derived value; computed at setup and on every change. createLazyComputed(fn) <T>(fn) => LazyComputed<T> A lazy derived value; marked dirty on change and computed when read ( value , peek , isDirty , dispose ). createSelection(fn) <T>(fn: () => T) => KeySelection<T> A keyed selection: isSelected(key) subscribes the binding that calls it only to that key; when the source changes, only the bindings of the old and the new value wake up. dispose() stops tracking. See: Reactivity . asReadonly(obj) <T>(o: T) => DeepReadonly<T> A live read-only view; reads are tracked, and writes and changing methods throw MJX212 . See: Reactivity . isReadonly(v) (v: unknown) => boolean true if the value is a view obtained with asReadonly . effect(fn, onValue?) (fn, cb?) => () => void A side effect; returns a stop function. onValue receives the return value of fn after every run, and reads inside it are not tracked. asyncTracking object The runtime helper the compiler uses to wrap the await s in a Virtualization dataRequest ( capture / suspend / resume / end ); not called by hand. See: Reactivity . untracked(fn) <T>(fn: () => T) => T A region without tracking; gives the return value of fn . effect calls inside it track as usual. deepClone(v) (v) => v A deep copy. clearModel(m) (m) => void Clears the reactive record. Signal<T> / Computed<T> / LazyComputed<T> class Fine-grained primitives. See: Reactivity .

title: API Reference
heading: Bindings — component.bindings
text: Method Description add(prop, source, member?, format?, formatInfo?) A one-way binding. formatInfo : { locale?, currency? } . model(source, member?, format?, formatInfo?) A two-way binding (based on the element type). model(getter, setter) A two-way binding with functions; x-model compiles to this. writeModel(value) Writes the value back to the model / x-model bindings on the component; true if it wrote (see Forms ). text(fn) / value(fn) A textContent / value binding. when(condFn, renderFn) Conditional content; the branch is rebuilt when the condition's value changes ( Object.is ; two falsy values count as the same). ternary(condFn, trueFn, falseFn) A two-branch condition; the branch is rebuilt when the condition's value changes ( Object.is ). list(itemsFn, renderFn) / loop(...) A list; rows are matched to the item object. switchCase(discFn, cases, defaultFn?) Multiple branches. method(fn) Reactive text / single content. watch(fn) A watcher cleaned up automatically. wait(fn) / display(fn) / html(fn) Waiting / visibility / innerHTML. remove(binding) Removes the binding from the collection and turns it off. See: Conditional Rendering and Lists , Forms and Two-Way Binding .

title: API Reference
heading: Dependency injection
text: Symbol Description ServiceCollection The registration collection ( addSingleton/addScoped/addTransient , tryAdd* , replace , remove , has ). ServiceProvider The resolver: get(token) is synchronous, getAsync(token) is for async factory/Promise registrations, createScope(name?) is a child scope, enableAutoDisposeTransients() disposes the transients in a child scope together with the scope, getAllServices() is the collection, dispose() . See: Resolving Services , Disposing Services . @Injectable(opts?) Marks the class for automatic registration; deps gives the constructor parameters in order, and startup: true creates the singleton inside app.run() . It is a standard (TC39) class decorator. inject(token) Resolves a dependency in a field initializer or the constructor of a class the provider builds; the return type comes from the token. FromService(token) Quick resolution from the application's provider; the return type is T | null : if it cannot resolve, it returns null and prints an MJX414 warning in development mode. If you are sure it is registered, write FromService(X)! . ServiceLifetime 'transient' \| 'singleton' \| 'scoped' . See: Introduction to Dependency Injection .

title: API Reference
heading: Routing
text: Symbol Description RouteItem The route definition type (one of control or redirect is required). RouteRedirect / RedirectTarget The redirect value ( string \| (to) => string ) and the { path, params, meta } passed to the function. RouterView The slot for a route's output ( name? ). RouterLink A link component with active/match classes (the default element is <a> ). Props: to , el , activeClass , exactClass , onActive / offActive , onExact / offExact , showHref , target , text , bypass (leaves the click to the browser). See: Links . NavigationDirection 'initial' \| 'push' \| 'replace' \| 'back' \| 'forward' \| 'traverse' . StackOptions The useRouter({ stack }) settings: retain , depth , persist , animation , duration , swipeBack . StackEntryInfo An item of app.router.stack : { index, uri, current, retained } . RouteInfo An item of app.router.routes : { fullPath, name, meta, route, chain } . StackTransitionContext The { direction, entering, leaving } a custom stack animation receives. title: API Reference
heading: Common helpers
text: Symbol Description dom DOM creation helpers: createElement(tag, options?) (a template element per tag is cached and cloned; options applies only on the first creation; 'text' gives a text node; MJX101 if there is no document ), createElementNS(ns, tag, options?) (error MJX103 ), createDocumentFragment() , createComment(text) , createTextNode(text) , querySelectorAll(selector) , convertToSvgElement(el) (recreates the element in the SVG namespace and puts it in its place), window , document , body . List , Dictionary , LinkedList Collection structures. See: Collections . Query<T> / Query.from(source) / Group<TKey, T> A chainable query wrapper ( where , select , orderBy , groupBy , first , any , aggregate , toArray …). See: Collection Queries (Query) . NameValuePair<K, V> A { Key, value } pair (an item of Dictionary ). See: Collections . NodeTypes Node type constants (an enum). Emitter<T> A typed event emitter: emitter.event(listener, thisArgs?, disposables?) subscribes and returns an IDisposable , fire(value) broadcasts, and dispose() closes it. A listener error goes to setUnexpectedErrorHandler . See: Error Handling . JSX The JSX type namespace ( JSX.Element , JSX.IntrinsicElements ); the compiler uses it for jsx-runtime . preProcessing(fn) Adds the callback to a permanent list and runs all the callbacks in the list right away; for one-time setups such as style injection. safeCall , safeCallAsync , safeCallSilent Error-safe call helpers. errorHandler / setUnexpectedErrorHandler(fn) The central error handler. errorHandler.addListener(fn) receives every error the framework reports as a MotifError . setUnexpectedErrorHandler(fn) receives only unexpected errors without a code (those caught inside safeCall / safeCallAsync and in Emitter listeners; these also go to the addListener listeners as they are); its default rethrows the error with setTimeout . Reports with a code ( MJX122 , MJX123 , MJX208 …) do not go to it. See: Error Handling , Error and Warning Codes . MotifError / MotifErrorCode The class of the errors the framework throws and reports; it carries a code (such as "MJX302" ) and an English message of the form [motifjs] MJX302: … , with the original error in cause if there is one. TransitionProps The transition configuration interface (a type). Bind<T> / toGetter(v) / read(v) The prop contract: T \| (() => T) ; toGetter turns it into a getter for live reading, and read gives the current value. Resilience Resilience helpers: Resilience.create.retry(...).timeout(...).execute(fn) (plus circuitBreaker , bulkhead , rateLimiter , fallback ). Its errors are MJX602 – MJX605 . See: Resilience . decorate(policy, fn) Wraps a resilience policy around a function: (ctx?) => policy.execute(fn, ctx) . ErrorHandler The class of the errorHandler instance: report(err) , addListener(fn) , setDevelopmentMode(b) , setConsoleLogging(b) , isDevelopment() , safeCall / safeCallSilent / wrapSafe / wrapSafeAsync .
