title: API Reference
heading: Developer tools
text: Symbol Description app.useReactiveMonitor(o) / configureReactivityLeakMonitor(o) Reactive dependency warnings: { enabled, threshold, name } is the leak watcher ( MJX507 when the number of effects tracking a field reaches threshold ), dependencies is the threshold for the dependencies an effect can collect in a single run (1000 by default, MJX209 when exceeded; 0 turns it off), and scans is the MJX210 check that catches at run time several instances of the same component type scanning the same list (on by default, false turns it off). debugGetDeps(target) / debugGetDepMap() Reactive dependency maps; from the @motifx/core/devtools subpath: import { debugGetDeps } from "@motifx/core/devtools" . registerDevtools(name, { describe?, inspect? }) A package opening its own state to DevTools; from the @motifx/core/devtools subpath. Returns { emit, pathOf, dispose } ( The DevTools Contract ). MotifDevtools , DevtoolsEvent The types of the globalThis.__MOTIF_DEVTOOLS__ object and its events; from the @motifx/core/devtools subpath ( The DevTools Contract ). DevtoolsTreeNode , DevtoolsPath , DevtoolsResult , DevtoolsComponentRef , DevtoolsStoreHolder , DevtoolsExtension , DevtoolsExtensionHandle The part types of the contract: a tree node, a path, a write result, a component reference, a store holder, an extension registration and the object the registration returns; from the @motifx/core/devtools subpath. nameModuleStore The call the compiler produces in a development build to name module stores; not called by hand ( The DevTools Contract ).

title: API Reference
heading: Special JSX attributes
text: Without JSX, the counterparts of these attributes are the keys of the props object and the component's calls (see Keys of the props object ). Attribute Description class / className Class (string/array/object/getter). style / x-style Style. on<event> A DOM event ( :once , :prevent , :stop , :capture , :passive , :self , :trusted ). on:name / on-name / on_name Attaches the handler as it is with motif.on("name", fn) (DOM and custom events; only the prefix is dropped, on-my-event → my-event ); parameter count ≤ 1 → fn(event) , 2+ → fn(sender, event) . ref / x-ref Captures the tag's component instance: ref={(c) => …} or ref={this.field} ( ref={field} in a function component), on every tag, exactly once; if both are written on the same tag, they run in source order. It works only on the component it is given to (the returned root in a function component); it is not part of props or this.props . For an inner item, use a separate prop name (e.g. inputRef ). initializeComponent Called once during setup with the tag's component (the same on plain DOM, class and function component tags; the returned root for a function). It runs together with the setup code the compiler produces. oninitializeComponent Called right after all initializeComponent code (the class method, the value on the tag, the one the compiler produced), before view() . Written as a class method or a tag prop; on a function component it is applied to the returned root. x-html Reactive innerHTML . x-wait / x-display / x-chunk Waiting / visibility / building the children in slices ( x-chunk : the frame time decides how many to build per frame; x-chunk={50} : 50 in the first round, then at least 50 children per frame). key Identifies a list item; checked for duplicates in development mode ( MJX202 ). Rows are matched by the item object, and key does not change how the DOM is reused. transition An enter/leave transition (a string or TransitionProps ). on<lifecycle> / x-<lifecycle> / x:<lifecycle> Lifecycle hooks; several spellings on the same tag are combined, and all of them run in source order. options={{ hideStrategy, disableDisposal, chunk }} The component's settings; copied into motif.options (on a plain DOM tag as well; no attribute is written). See: Lifecycle . Attributes named after methods focus , blur , click , select , scrollTo / scrollBy / scrollIntoView , show , showModal , close , showPopover , hidePopover , togglePopover , requestSubmit , checkValidity , reportValidity , showPicker , load , setSelectionRange , setRangeText , setPointerCapture , releasePointerCapture , fastSeek … call the element's method of the same name, and no attribute is written; if a getter is given, it is called again on every change. show / showModal / showPopover open with true and close with false ( close() / hidePopover() ); togglePopover passes the boolean on; methods such as close , requestSubmit and load are called on a truthy value; methods with arguments such as setSelectionRange take the value as their argument (an array → an argument list). See: JSX and Templates .

title: API Reference
heading: Error and warning codes
text: Every MJX code, its console message and its meaning are on the Error and Warning Codes page.

title: API Reference
heading: Next step
text: For the full list of codes, go on to Error and Warning Codes .

title: Error and Warning Codes
text: Every message the framework and the compiler produce carries an MJX code and appears in the console in the form [motifjs] MJX302: Named route 'note' was not found. . The message texts are in English and may change; in your code, branch on the code, not on the message. How errors are thrown, reported and listened to is on the Error Handling page. Kind What happens thrown Returns to the caller as a MotifError ; caught with try/catch or .catch . reported Written to the console with errorHandler.report ( app.useLogging(false) turns it off) and goes to the errorHandler.addListener listeners; the original error is in cause . Works in production too. warning Written to the console and the DevTools warning list only in development mode ( app.useDevelopment(true) ). value The error comes back as a value or is given to a callback; it is neither thrown nor reported. Lazy error Given to onError as a Lazy loading error. compile error / warning Produced by @motifx/compiler during compilation; an error stops the build, and a warning is written to the terminal. motif-lint A finding of the type-aware checking tool. The places shown with ‹…› in the message column are filled with the value at run time.

title: Error and Warning Codes
heading: Compiler
text: MJX001 – MJX018 belong to the compiler and motif-lint . Explanations with examples are in the Compile-time warnings section. Code Kind Message Meaning MJX001 compile warning In a block-bodied function in JSX child position the condition is moved out of the closure; … A local variable defined inside a block-bodied getter with parameters is not visible in the branches. MJX002 compile warning "‹name›" is a DOM event name; on a component tag it is bound as a DOM listener … The camelCase spelling of a DOM event name on a component tag; it does not reach the props. MJX003 compile warning List item has no "key". … A list item built with .map() / .forEach() has no key . MJX004 compile warning "‹method›()" looks an item up by "‹field›" by scanning a reactive list inside a reactive getter … A reactive list is scanned inside a reactive getter with find / findIndex / some / every and a predicate of the form x.field === value ; if many components do this, every change means n² reads. Take the element from a keyed map, or read it with untracked . See The trap of every row scanning the list . MJX005 motif-lint <‹tag› ‹prop›={… ? … : …}>: the component declares "‹prop›" as "‹type›" … The type of a prop given a ternary does not accept a function; declare the prop as Bind<T> . MJX006 compile error Directive "‹name›" is not supported. … An unsupported directive. MJX007 compile warning Unknown directive "‹name›": it is passed on as the prop "on‹name›". … An unrecognized x- name. MJX008 compile error A function expression cannot be a JSX child; use an arrow function: {() => …}. function () { … } in child position. MJX009 compile error Event handler "‹name›" must be a function; … A string or boolean value on a DOM event. MJX010 compile error Lifecycle hook "‹name›" must be a function, a list of functions, or a reference to one; … A value that cannot be called on a lifecycle hook. MJX011 compile error Directive "‹name›" does not accept this value; … A value that cannot be turned into a getter on x-text , x-html , x-value , x-model or x-watch . MJX012 compile error Directive "‹name›" does not accept an object literal. / Directive "‹name›" expects a number or no value: x-chunk or x-chunk={200}. An object literal on x-wait / x-display ; a value that cannot be a number on x-chunk (a string, an object, an arrow function). MJX013 compile error Unsupported JSX tag name: ‹type›. / Unsupported JSX child: ‹type›. An unsupported JSX form. MJX014 motif-lint error Cannot read ‹configFile›: ‹message› motif-lint could not read the tsconfig file. MJX015 compile warning, motif-lint ‹class›.‹member› overrides a ComponentBase member and does not call super.‹member›(…); … A member that overrides a ComponentBase member ends without reaching super . MJX016 compile warning A "switch" getter in JSX child position is not lowered to bindings.switchCase … / A block-bodied getter returning a ternary is not lowered … A switch or ternary getter could not be turned into switchCase / ternary ; the content is rebuilt on every change. MJX017 compile warning A reactive getter writes "‹target›" (‹op›): a getter that writes what it reads retriggers itself … A reactive getter (a JSX getter, an attribute getter, a directive, effect , createComputed , bindings.* ) writes a reactive value it reads: ++ , a compound assignment, or an assignment to a field it reads elsewhere; a getter that writes what it reads triggers itself ( MJX203 ). Writing to a field it does not read, and to a plain class field, does not warn. Move the write into an event handler or a method; if it has to stay, put the read of that value inside untracked so the getter does not subscribe to it (the whole expression for x++ and compound assignment). MJX018 compile warning "‹method›()" changes the reactive list "‹list›" in place inside a reactive getter … A reactive list is changed in place inside a reactive getter: sort / reverse always, and push / pop / shift / unshift / splice if the getter also reads the list; a getter that reads the list triggers itself. Work on a copy ( [...list].sort(...) ), or keep the result in a field or a computed.

title: Error and Warning Codes
heading: Components and the DOM
text: Code Kind Message Meaning MJX101 thrown dom.createElement('‹tag›'): no document is available (no DOM environment). There is no document while an element is being created; the code is running without a DOM environment. MJX102 thrown Invalid element selector "‹description›". An invalid element selector. MJX103 reported dom.createElementNS('‹tag›') failed. createElementNS failed. MJX104 warning Skipped inserting a component into the DOM because it contains its own parent. A component that contains its own parent was not added to the DOM. MJX105 reported Applying router link classes failed. The route link classes could not be applied. MJX106 warning The placeholder parent changed; rebuilding the component. The placeholder's parent changed; the component is being rebuilt. MJX107 reported Disposing a child component failed. A child component could not be disposed. MJX108 value Component is disposed; the result of doWork was discarded. The result of doWork was dropped because the component was disposed; doWork resolves with this MotifError , and if the given promise was rejected, the rejection is in cause (see doWork ). MJX109 warning Content block is disposed; its child was removed from the content body. While a ContentBlock was being disposed, one of its parts in the body was removed and disposed; one warning per part (see ContentBody and ContentBlock ). MJX110 Lazy error Lazy timeout: the component did not load within ‹ms› ms. The Lazy load did not finish within timeoutMs ; the error is given to onError , and then Fallbackview is shown. MJX111 Lazy error Lazy aborted: loading the component was cancelled. The Lazy load was cancelled with signal ; it is given to onError and not reported. MJX112 reported resolveComponent: the factory chain exceeded ‹depth› levels; a factory may be returning itself. The resolveComponent factory chain went over 100 levels; a factory may be returning itself. MJX113 thrown The transport slot has no parent; mount the slot before transporting into it. The transport slot has no parent; place the slot before moving content into it. MJX114 reported Placing the navigation target into its host failed. The navigation target could not be placed in its container. MJX115 reported Disposing the previous navigation target failed. The previous navigation target could not be disposed. MJX116 value Timeout: the listener guard did not settle within ‹ms› ms. A listener guard did not settle within timeoutMs ; the guard is rejected with this MotifError . MJX117 reported Detaching a control failed. A control could not be detached. MJX118 reported The onRemove callback failed while detaching a control. The onRemove callback failed while a control was being detached. MJX119 reported Moving a fragment's DOM range stopped: its end marker was not found (possible infinite loop). While a fragment's DOM range was being moved, its closing marker could not be found. MJX120 reported Scanning a fragment's DOM range stopped: its end marker was not found (possible infinite loop). While a fragment's DOM range was being scanned, its closing marker could not be found. MJX121 warning This code was compiled for compiler contract ‹compiled›, but the @motifx/core runtime implements contract ‹runtime›. Install matching versions of @motifx/compiler and @motifx/core, and rebuild packages that ship compiled JSX. The code was compiled with a compiler contract the core does not support. Bring @motifx/compiler and @motifx/core to matching versions, and rebuild packages that carry compiled JSX. MJX122 reported The component ‹hook› hook threw. A component hook ( onConfig , onBuilt , onMounted , initializeComponent , ref …) or a motif.on("x:…") listener threw, or the promise it returned was rejected; the component keeps being built (see Where errors are caught ). MJX123 reported The '‹event›' event handler threw. An event handler ( onclick , motif.on ) or an application event listener ( app.on , onRouterChanged ) threw, or the promise it returned was rejected; the other handlers of the same event run. MJX124 warning A spread object on a DOM tag cannot set ‹key›; the key was ignored. Write it on the tag, or use x-html, for HTML you trust. An object spread onto a plain DOM tag contains innerHTML or srcdoc ; it was not written. For HTML you trust, use x-html or a value written directly on the tag. MJX125 warning A spread object on a DOM tag cannot set a javascript: URL on '‹key›'; the value was ignored. Write the attribute on the tag if it is intended. An object spread onto a plain DOM tag contains a javascript: address for a link attribute; it was not written. Write a link you mean on purpose directly on the tag. MJX126 reported Lazy: loading the component failed and no Fallbackview is set; the host was cleared. The Lazy load failed and there is no Fallbackview ; the container was emptied. The original error is in cause . MJX127 thrown The loaded module has no default export. … / The loaded value is not a component (got ‹got›). … A lazy route or Lazy loaded a module without a default export, or a value that is not a component. In the router it becomes the cause of the MJX304 report, and in Lazy it counts as a loading error. MJX128 warning ‹cls› overrides ‹member› without calling super.‹member› … / ‹cls› defines '‹member›' as an instance field … / ‹cls› replaces '‹member›' … A class component hides a ComponentBase member: an override that does not call super , an instance field that hides a method, or a value put in place of a member the framework sets up. Reported once per class (see Names of class members ). MJX129 reported The ‹callback› callback given to using threw. The onfulfilled or onrejected handler given to using threw, or the promise it returned was rejected. The original error is in cause (see using ). MJX130 reported Building a chunked child failed. A child chunked with x-chunk threw while being built when its turn came; the other children in the chunk keep being built. The .map row that failed is tried again on the list's next update. The original error is in cause (see Large lists ).

title: Error and Warning Codes
heading: Reactivity, bindings and lists
text: Code Kind Message Meaning MJX201 thrown ListBinding: renderFn must return a component instance, a component class, or a factory function. The list binding's renderFn did not return a component, a component class or a factory. MJX202 warning ListBinding: duplicate key "‹key›" at index ‹index›. Rows are matched by the item object, not by key, so rendering is not affected; keep keys unique so they identify items. A duplicate key was seen while the list was updating. Rows are matched by the item object, so rendering is not affected; keep the key s unique. MJX203 warning An effect ran ‹max› times in one flush and keeps triggering itself; it is skipped for the rest of this flush. It probably writes a value it reads (for example state.n++). Wrap the write in untracked(...). An effect kept triggering itself in a flush and was skipped for the rest of that flush; it may be writing a value it reads. Put the write inside untracked(...) . MJX204 warning A component reached a text binding and was not written to the DOM. For a template prop that can change later, write a getter: {() => props.tpl}. Templates that are ready at setup also work as {props.tpl}. A component ended up in a text binding and was not written to the DOM. MJX205 reported Virtualization: the watch callback threw. The Virtualization watch callback threw. MJX206 warning Virtualization: autoRefresh stopped; dataRequest may be changing the reactive data it reads on every refresh. Virtualization autoRefresh was stopped; dataRequest may be changing the reactive data it reads. MJX207 reported Virtualization: loading data failed. The Virtualization data could not be loaded (the next page request included). MJX208 reported An effect threw. An effect or a binding function threw; the other effects in the same flush run, and the binding keeps its last healthy state. MJX209 warning An effect tracked ‹count› dependencies in one run (limit ‹limit›), owner ‹owner›. It reads many values one by one, probably a reactive list item by item; look items up by key or read the list with untracked(...). useReactiveMonitor({ dependencies }) sets the limit. An effect collected more dependencies in a single run than the threshold (1000 by default); once per effect, and at most ten times per session. With DevTools open, the owning component and binding are written. Usually a reactive list is being scanned from start to end in every row: find the element by key, or read the list with untracked . app.useReactiveMonitor({ dependencies: 2000 }) changes the threshold, and 0 turns it off. See The trap of every row scanning the list . MJX210 warning "‹method›()" scans a reactive list of ‹count› items from ‹who›: a change to the fields they read reruns all of them and each rereads the list … Two or more instances of the same component type (and binding) scan the same reactive list with find / findIndex / findLast / findLastIndex / some / every , and the list has at least as many items as there are instances; it is caught even if the list comes from props, from another file or from a service, and a plain array does not warn because it is not tracked. Instances are counted by component object, and two bindings of the same instance count as one instance; a hundred rows scanning a three-item settings list does not warn; for effects without an owner ( createComputed , a plain effect ) the threshold is eight effects. Once per list, and at most ten times per session; with DevTools closed the owner is unknown, so the check does not run. Read the element from a keyed Map or a computed index in the store, or take the list with untracked . useReactiveMonitor({ scans: false }) turns it off. MJX211 warning Operation ‹id› (‹kind› ‹name›) was resumed after it ended; its writes are still recorded under it. End an operation after its last write, or use startOperation/endOperation for work that spans callbacks. A DevTools operation that had ended was resumed with resumeOperation ; the writes made meanwhile are still recorded under that operation. Once per operation, in development only. End the operation after its last write; for work that spans callbacks, use startOperation / endOperation . See DevTools for Packages . MJX212 thrown Cannot ‹action›: this is a read-only view made with asReadonly(). Change the data through the reactive object the view was made from. A view obtained with asReadonly was written to, a field was deleted from it, or an array-changing method ( push , splice , sort , …) or a Map / Set change ( set , add , delete , clear ) was called on it. The operation is not carried out and the data does not change. Make the change through the reactive object the view was taken from. See A read-only view .

title: Error and Warning Codes
heading: Routing
text: Code Kind Message Meaning MJX301 warning RouterView outlet '‹outlet›' was not built within ‹ms› ms, so the route chain cannot be mounted. Does the layout component render a <RouterView>? The RouterView outlet was not built in time; the route chain could not be placed. MJX302 thrown Named route '‹name›' was not found. The named route was not found ( navigateByName , href , evict ). title: Error and Warning Codes
heading: Next step
text: For filtering, sorting and grouping arrays, go on to Collection Queries .

title: Collection Queries (Query)
text: Query<T> is a small wrapper for querying an array, or any iterable source, with chained steps. Filtering, transforming, sorting and grouping steps are written readably in a single chain: Query is optional: it goes into the bundle only when you import it, and it changes no global object, Array.prototype included. A query always starts with Query.from(...) .

title: Collection Queries (Query)
heading: Creating a query
text: Form Description Query.from(source) Produces a query from the source. new Query(source) The same as Query.from . source can be an array or any Iterable<T> : a Set , Map.keys() , Map.values() , generator functions, reactive arrays. If the source is an array, it is not copied but read directly; other iterables are copied into an array at the moment of Query.from . The source array is not changed by any step.

title: Collection Queries (Query)
heading: Chained steps
text: These methods return a new Query ; another step can be added after them. Method Description where(predicate) Keeps the items that satisfy the condition. predicate(item, index) . select(selector) Transforms each item. selector(item, index) . orderBy(keySelector) Sorts ascending by key. orderByDescending(keySelector) Sorts descending by key. distinctBy(keySelector) Keeps only the first of the items that share a key. groupBy(keySelector) Splits the items into { key, items } groups; the result is a Query<Group<TKey, T>> .

title: Collection Queries (Query)
heading: Methods that produce a result
text: These methods end the chain and return a value. Method Returns Description toArray() T[] Copies the result into a new array. first() T The first item; throws a MotifError ( MJX601 ) if the query is empty. firstOrDefault() T \| undefined The first item; undefined if the query is empty. any(predicate?) boolean Without a condition, "is there at least one item"; with one, "is there an item that satisfies the condition". all(predicate) boolean Whether every item satisfies the condition. aggregate(seed, func) TResult Reduces the items to a single value, starting from the seed value. Query is iterable, so it can be walked directly without calling toArray() :

title: Collection Queries (Query)
heading: Sorting
text: The sort is stable: items with equal keys keep their order from the source. Keys are compared with < and > ; number, string and Date keys work as expected. Strings are sorted by character code; if you need a language's alphabetical order (Turkish, for example, where ç and ş belong right after c and s ), sort the result yourself:

title: Collection Queries (Query)
heading: Grouping
text: The groups come in the order in which their key first appears in the source. Key equality follows the rules of Map ; object keys are grouped by reference, not by value.

title: Collection Queries (Query)
heading: Use with reactivity
text: Query reads reactive arrays with ordinary array methods, so when it is used inside a getter, a createComputed or an effect , a dependency on the source is set up and the result is recomputed when the source changes. In a list, the query is put in a getter and the rows are drawn with a list binding. In JSX the compiler turns the expression this.recent.map(...) ( recent().map(...) in a function) into bindings.list , and without JSX bindings.list is called directly. Rows are matched to the item object, and the DOM nodes of the same object are reused; key takes no part in this matching, it identifies the item (see Conditional Rendering and Lists ). The list in the example shows the five most recently edited notes: When a note is edited and its updatedAt changes, or when it is archived, the chain runs from the start and the list applies only the difference to the DOM. For very large lists, use the Virtualization component from the Virtual Lists section.

title: Collection Queries (Query)
heading: Things to know
text: Evaluation is immediate. Every step of the chain produces its own intermediate array; there is no lazy evaluation. Up to a few thousand items, the cost of this is negligible. The source does not change. orderBy and orderByDescending sort a copy of the source; toArray() returns a new array on every call. The result is a snapshot. Every step runs at the moment it is called; items added to the source later do not show up in step results computed earlier. ( Query.from(array) with no steps applied does not copy the array, so it reads the array's current state; a source that is not an array is copied at the moment of from .) For an up-to-date result, set up the chain inside a getter and run it again on every read. The chain returns Query . The result of steps such as where , select and groupBy is a Query , not an array ( groupBy → Query<Group<TKey, T>> ); where an array is needed, add toArray() at the end.

title: Collection Queries (Query)
heading: Next step
text: For the List , Dictionary and LinkedList structures, go on to Collections .

title: Collections
text: The core exports three small collection classes. They are not reactive; for a reactive list use reactive([]) ( Reactivity ). For querying, see Collection Queries .

title: Collections
heading: List<T>
text: An array wrapper that gives add/remove events and does membership checks backed by a Set . In the example, the list keeps the ids of the open notes: Member Description Add(item) Appends at the end and returns the index; ItemAdded(item) is called. AddBefore(item) Adds at the front; ItemAddedBefore(item) is called. The return value is newLength − 1 (not the index of the added item). Insert(index, item) Inserts at the given index; ItemSplice(index, item) is called. Returns the empty array that splice returns. remove(item) Removes the item and returns the removed item as a one-element array; if the item is not in the list, it does nothing and returns an empty array. removeIndex(index) Removes the item at the index; returns the removed items as an array. clear() Removes everything; returns the new, empty inner array. has(item) / indexOf(item) / item(index) Membership ( Set , O(1)) / index / the item at an index. FindFromKey(key, value) The items where item[key] === value . forEach(fn) / filter(fn) The array counterparts; filter returns a new array. ReverseClone() Returns a reversed copy of the items; the list's order does not change. items / count The inner array / the length. Dispose() Empties the inner array (the Set is kept). ItemAdded , ItemAddedBefore , ItemSplice Assignable callbacks; called after the corresponding addition. Removals give no events. items gives the inner array; if it is changed from outside, it gets out of step with has .

title: Collections
heading: Dictionary<K, V> and NameValuePair<K, V>
text: A key-value dictionary that keeps NameValuePair pairs in a List . Keys are compared with == , and lookup is linear. In the example, the dictionary keeps unsaved drafts by note id: Member Description Add(key, value) Adds a pair (the same key can repeat; there is no check), returns the index from List.Add ; OnItemAdded(key, value) is called. has(key) Whether the key exists ( == ). item(key) The first matching NameValuePair , or undefined . remove(key) Removes all pairs whose key matches. removeIndex(index) Removes the pair at the index (zero-based); returns the removed pairs as an array. clear() Removes everything. forEach(fn) / filter(fn) / find(fn) Walking, filtering and finding over the NameValuePair s. values The underlying List<NameValuePair<K, V>> . OnItemAdded An assignable callback. NameValuePair<K, V> is a plain class with two fields: Key (capital K) and value .

title: Collections
heading: LinkedList<T>
text: A doubly linked, circular list. The add operations return a function that cuts the link ; it is designed for "add, then remove with the handle in hand" patterns such as listener lists. In the example, the list keeps cleanup functions to be run later: Member Description push(value) / unshift(value) Adds at the end / at the front; returns a function that removes that node (calling it again does nothing). pop() / shift() Removes from the end / from the front and returns the value; undefined if empty. clear() Removes everything; removal functions obtained earlier stop having any effect. size / isEmpty() The number of elements / whether it is empty. [Symbol.iterator] Walks from start to end ( for…of , spreading). Removing while walking is safe; an added item may be seen in that same walk. There is no index access; if you need access by index, use List or a plain array.

title: Collections
heading: See also
text: API Reference , Collection Queries .

title: Collections
heading: Next step
text: For a container that places and swaps a single piece of dynamic content, go on to Frame .

title: Frame
text: Conditional branches ( && , the ternary operator, switch ), getter children of the form {() => expression} and route pages all work on the same structure: a container that holds a single piece of content and swaps it . That container is Frame . Frame is a component whose root is a comment node (it adds no element to the DOM); at any moment it holds at most one piece of content (a component or an array of components), the content is changed with navigate , and the old content is disposed.

title: Frame
heading: Usage
text: The summary panel in the example switches between the recent notes list ( RecentNotes ) and the folder chart ( FolderChart ) with two buttons: Children written between <Frame>…</Frame> in JSX, and those given with new Frame({ childs: [...] }) without JSX, become the first content. If a Promise is given to navigate , the content is loaded with Lazy .

title: Frame
heading: API
text: Member Description new Frame(props?) An empty container. If props.childs is given ( <Frame>…</Frame> in JSX), the children are added as the first content. navigate(page, keepOldControl?) page can be a component, an array of components, a component class/factory or a Promise . The old content is disposed (it stays in place if keepOldControl: true is given), and the new one is added. If a Promise is given, the content is loaded with Lazy ; the next navigate cancels the previous load. A second call with the same content does nothing. The Promise it returns resolves once the content is in place. navigateLazy(caller, options?, keepOldControl?) A shorthand for navigate(Lazy({ caller, options })) . flush() Disposes the current content; the container stays empty. motif.clear() does the same job. current The content shown ( ComponentBase , an array, or null ). isBusy true while a navigate is in progress. dispose(options?) Disposes the content first, then the container; options is passed on to the content too.

title: Frame
heading: Timing
text: The first content is synchronous. While the container is empty and page is not a Promise , the content is in place by the time navigate returns; when build() completes, the first branch is on screen (see Conditional rendering - Synchronous first render ). Later changes are queued. Consecutive navigate calls are queued behind a lock, and each waits for the previous one to finish. A new call that comes in between drops the result of an older call that has not been placed yet (only the content requested last is placed). Old content without a leave transition is disposed ( onDisposed ) before the new content is added. If the content cannot be placed, MJX114 is reported, and if the old content cannot be disposed, MJX115 ; the container keeps working.

title: Frame
heading: Leave and enter transitions
text: The old content plays its leave transition: first its running animations are cancelled, then it is disposed with dispose({ deep: true }) ; if a leave transition is defined (the transition prop or motif.options.transition.out(...) ), it plays. The new content does not wait for the old one to finish: while the old content leaves, the new one is added right away, and their order is decided by the mode of the nearest element parent (see Styling and animation - Enter and leave order ): mode Behaviour 'concurrent' (default) While the old content leaves, the new content enters at the same time. 'out-in' The new content is not placed in the DOM until the old one's leave finishes. 'in-out' The old one's leave is postponed until the new one's enter finishes. Frame has a comment node, so it does not carry the mode itself; it uses that of its nearest element parent. A conditional branch inside an element that carries the mode also passes through the nested Frame s and uses the same mode. dispose() , flush() and motif.clear() also play the content's leave transition and wait for it to finish; dispose({ skipLeaveTransition: true }) is passed on to the content with the same option.

title: Frame
heading: Where the framework sets up a Frame
text: The framework sets up a Frame itself in these places: {condition && <X/>} ( bindings.when ), the ternary operator ( bindings.ternary ), switch ( bindings.switchCase ), {() => …} children that return a component ( bindings.method ), and Lazy . RouterView is a separate component, but it uses the same navigation logic on a page change (the queue lock, Lazy for a Promise ); the difference is that it does not wait for the leaving page to be disposed (see The page that leaves ). Apart from that, the rules above apply to all of them.

title: Frame
heading: Next step
text: For content through a dynamic import() , see Lazy ; for the usage side of branch changes, Conditional Rendering and Lists .

title: Lazy
text: Lazy calls a function that produces a Promise , turns the result into a component and places it in a Frame . It is designed for code splitting ( () => import('./X') ), but it works with any Promise .

title: Lazy
heading: Usage
text: In the example, the folder chart is loaded lazily so that Chart.js is downloaded only when needed. The component is a named export, so mapResult picks it from the module: Lazy is a function; a Lazy({ caller, options }) call returns the same Frame and can be placed with controls.add . frame.navigateLazy(caller, options) and frame.navigate(promise) use the same path.

title: Lazy
heading: The loading flow
text: Placeholderview (or Loaderview if there is none) is shown right away. caller() is called right away (it does not wait for the component to enter the DOM). If timeoutMs is given, the load counts as failed with MJX110 when the time is up; if signal is given, abort() cuts the load off with MJX111 . A successful result is turned into a component with mapResult . The default converter takes the module's default export (for the result of import() ); if another export is needed, write mapResult: (m) => m.FolderChart as in the example. If the returned value is a class it is built with new , and if it is a function it is built by calling it; a ready instance is used as it is (no props are given). An Options API object or factory is turned into a component as well. A module without a default export, or some other object that is not a component, makes the load fail with MJX127 and moves on to step 5. null keeps the loading view, text is placed as a text node, and a promise or an array is placed as it resolves. If minDelayMs is given and the load finished sooner, the remaining time is waited out (this keeps the loading view from flashing on short loads). Then the content is placed in the Frame ; Loaderview plays its leave transition and is disposed. On failure, onError(err) is called first. If there is a Fallbackview , it is shown and the error stays there (it is not reported). Otherwise the container is emptied and the error is reported as MJX126 with errorHandler.report — it is written to console.error and goes to the errorHandler.addListener listeners, with the original error in the cause field (see Error handling - Listening for reports ). Having given onError does not remove the report. For a cancelled ( signal ) load, onError is called once with MJX111 ; it makes no difference whether the cancellation arrives during an attempt or while waiting to retry. Fallbackview is not shown, the content does not change and no report is written. When the container is disposed, everything stops at the first moment of disposal: running timers and pending retries are cleared, onError is not called, no report is written, a load that finishes later is ignored and nothing is built.

title: Lazy
heading: Options ( LazyOptions<T> )
text: Option Type Description Loaderview ComponentBase The content shown while loading is in progress. Placeholderview ComponentBase Takes precedence over Loaderview ; when both are given, only this one is shown. Fallbackview ComponentBase The content shown when the last attempt also fails. minDelayMs number The minimum time that must pass before the content is placed. timeoutMs number The upper limit of each attempt; MJX110 when exceeded. signal AbortSignal Cancelling the load from outside; MJX111 . Frame.navigate(promise) gives this itself. mapResult (result) => component Turns the load result into a component; the default export by default. onError (error) => void When the last attempt also fails, and on cancellation ( MJX111 ), before Fallbackview ; not called during disposal. retry number \| LazyRetryOptions Retrying (below). onRetry (attempt, error) => void Before every retry; attempt starts at 1.

title: Lazy
heading: Retrying — retry
text: It is retried count times; total attempts are count + 1 . The wait grows with each attempt: delayMs × attempt (500, 1000, 1500…). With whenOnline: true , if the device is offline ( navigator.onLine === false ), the counter does not start; the wait begins when the online event arrives. If signal is cancelled during the wait, the attempt is dropped and onError is called with MJX111 ; if the container is disposed, the attempt is dropped quietly. timeoutMs applies to each attempt separately.

title: Lazy
heading: In route pages
text: control: () => import('./pages/X') in a route definition and fallbacks.notFound/error use their own lazy loading path; the Lazy options (loading view, retries) do not apply there. To lazily load a heavy part inside a page, use Lazy (see The Route Table - Lazy loading ).

title: Lazy
heading: Next step
text: To show content in another slot, go on to Transport and TransportTo . For the framework's error reporting model, see Error Handling ; for the container's timing rules, Frame .

title: Transport and TransportTo
text: Used to show a component's content somewhere outside its own tree. The typical example: page-specific command buttons appearing in the layout's top bar. It is made of two parts: Transport — the target slot . It is put in the layout (or anywhere the content should appear). TransportTo — the sender . Content written between its tags is moved to the slot of the same name.

title: Transport and TransportTo
heading: Usage
text: In the example the top bar carries a slot, and the pin button of the open note is sent to that slot from the note page. The slot: The sender: The layout places the bar with <PageBar /> , and the note page places the button with <PinAction note={note} /> . The layout places the bar with new PageBar() , and the note page places the button with new PinAction({ note }) . The layout places the bar with motifComponent(PageBar) , and the note page places the button with motifComponent(PinAction, { note }) . Transport and TransportTo are classes of the core. Without JSX, the slot is built with new Transport({ name }) , and the sender, as the compiler would produce it, with motifComponent(TransportTo, { name, childs }) .

title: Transport and TransportTo
heading: Props
text: Component Prop Description Transport name The slot's name (required). Transport mode 'replace' (the default) or 'merge' ; see Several senders in a slot . TransportTo name The name of the slot the content is sent to.

title: Transport and TransportTo
heading: Behaviour
text: Order does not matter. The slot can be created before or after; if a TransportTo is set up while the slot does not exist yet, the content is moved the moment the slot registers. The content stays tied to the sending component. The bindings and event handlers on the moved elements keep working with the state of the component they were written in; in the example, when the note is pinned, the text of the button in the slot changes too. The lifetime belongs to the sender. When the TransportTo is disposed, the content it carried is removed from the slot and disposed. When leaving a route page, the content leaves the slot right away, without waiting for the page to be disposed (see The page that leaves ); in uses such as a command bar, the content swaps places with the new page's on its own. If the slot is removed, the content goes too. When the slot is disposed, the moved content inside it is disposed as well; even if a slot with the same name is created again, the content does not come back. Children added later are moved too. A component added later to the controls collection of the TransportTo goes straight to the slot if the slot exists; it stays live like the first children, and goes away with them when the sender is disposed. The sender's controladded event fires for each child. The Transport slot itself is a fragment (it adds no element to the DOM; the content sits where the slot is). TransportTo leaves an empty <div> where it is; the content appears in the slot, not there. Both communicate through application events, so they must be used inside a running Application . If a second Transport with the same name is set up, the registration moves to the new one, and the senders move their content to the new slot.

title: Transport and TransportTo
heading: Several senders in a slot — mode
text: When several TransportTo s send content to the same slot, mode decides. Whether the slot is set up before or after the senders does not change the result: 'replace' (the default): only the content of the sender set up last stays in the slot. The previous content in the slot is removed and disposed; it does not come back even if that sender closes. 'merge' : the content of all senders is added to the slot in the order they were set up; when each sender closes, only its own content goes away. If you want an area that several blocks fill together and that piles up in a body, ContentBody and ContentBlock are designed for that.

title: Transport and TransportTo
heading: Moving in code — Transporter
text: The helper under the Transport / TransportTo pair is public; it is used to move a component to another parent without JSX: transport detaches the child from its old parent without playing a leave transition, adds it to the new parent's controls and activates its bindings again ( reState ). TransportOptions : index (the insertion index; transportMany places the children in the given order starting from this index), keepState: true (do not activate the bindings again), owner (writes the mover into motif.options.ownerTransporter ). If the child is already in that parent, it does nothing.

title: Transport and TransportTo
heading: Next step
text: For a body that fills up by piling content from several sources, see ContentBody and ContentBlock ; for the rest of the controls collection, Components - controls .

title: ContentBody and ContentBlock
text: Transport shows a single sender's content in a slot; ContentBody , on the other hand, is a body that several blocks fill together . A body is opened in the layout, blocks in different places on the page add their parts to it, and the parts pile up in the body.

title: ContentBody and ContentBlock
heading: Usage
text: In the example the layout's bottom bar opens a body; the folder list adds the total number of notes to it, and the note page adds the edit time of the open note. The body: The blocks: The layout places the bottom bar with <StatusBar /> , the folder list with <CountStatus /> , and the note page with <EditedStatus note={note} /> . The layout places the bottom bar with new StatusBar() , the folder list with new CountStatus() , and the note page with new EditedStatus({ note }) . The layout places the bottom bar with motifComponent(StatusBar) , the folder list with motifComponent(CountStatus) , and the note page with motifComponent(EditedStatus, { note }) . ContentBody and ContentBlock are classes of the core. Without JSX, the body is built with new ContentBody({ name }) , and a block, as the compiler would produce it, with motifComponent(ContentBlock, { target, childs }) . While the note page is open, two parts sit side by side in the bar: the number of notes and the edit time. Both are updated by the binding of the component they were written in. When the page closes, only its part goes away; the folder list's part stays.

title: ContentBody and ContentBlock
heading: Props
text: Component Prop Description ContentBody name The body's name. If a second body with the same name is set up, new blocks go to it; disposing the old body later does not spoil the new body's registration. ContentBlock target The name of the body the parts are added to.

title: ContentBody and ContentBlock
heading: Behaviour
text: Both are fragment-rooted; they add no element where they are. While the target body exists, a block does not build its children itself : every child added (the childs given with the block, and those that arrive later with controls.add ) is moved to the body's controls at that moment and built there; its parent becomes the body. childs are moved in the block's constructor, before the block is built. The block's controladded event fires for each child. If the body does not exist yet, the children the block has while it is being built are built together with the block and appear in the block's place; those added with controls.add after the block is built wait without being built. The moment a body with the same name is created, all of them are moved to the body; the final placement does not depend on the order. Parts pile up in the body; each block knows only the parts it added itself. When a block is disposed, it removes and disposes its own parts in the body (in development mode an MJX109 warning is written for each part); the other blocks' parts stay. When the body is disposed, all the parts inside it are disposed with it; the blocks are not informed, and even if a new body with the same name is set up, the parts do not come back. The bindings and event handlers of the moved parts keep working with the state of the component they were written in. The body and the blocks communicate through the application's events, so they are used inside an Application that has been set up. A body created before the application is set up gives an error.

title: ContentBody and ContentBlock
heading: Comparison with Transport
text: Transport / TransportTo ContentBody / ContentBlock Purpose Showing a sender's content in a slot Piling up the parts of many blocks in a body Several sources mode: 'replace' keeps the last one; 'merge' combines them Always piles up When the sender is disposed Removes its own content Removes its own parts ( MJX109 ) Placement The slot is a fragment, the sender leaves an empty <div> Both are fragments

title: ContentBody and ContentBlock
heading: Next step
text: To show large lists with virtual scrolling, go on to Virtual Lists (Virtualization) . For a single-sender slot and moving in code, see Transport and TransportTo ; for the basics of the component tree, Components .

title: Virtual Lists (Virtualization)
text: In lists of thousands of items, putting every item in the DOM hurts performance. MotifJS's Virtualization component shows lists whose row height is fixed or can be calculated in advance efficiently, by keeping only the visible items (and a few buffer rows on either side) in the DOM. It asks for the data page by page itself.

title: Virtual Lists (Virtualization)
heading: Basic usage
text: In the example, a folder's list of notes is drawn with a virtual list. The data is sliced page by page from the notes in the service, and each row is the note row component : The folder layout places the list together with the search state with <NoteList folder={this.folder} state={this.state} /> . The folder layout places the list together with the search state with new NoteList({ folder: this.folder, state: this.state }) . The folder layout places the list together with the search state with motifComponent(NoteList, { folder: this.folder, state: this.state }) . When mainTemplate is not given, the list sets up its root div with overflow-y: auto; height: 100%; position: relative; overflow-anchor: none and scrolls inside itself, so the container that holds it must have a height, or the height is given to the list with style . dataRequest reads the search text and the notes, so the list refreshes on its own as you type into the search box (see Automatic refresh ).

title: Virtual Lists (Virtualization)
heading: Props ( VirtualizationProps<T> )
text: Prop Type Description dataRequest (req) => Promise<VirtualizationDataResponse<T>> Required. The function that fetches a page of data; see The dataRequest contract . itemTemplate (item: T, index: number) => any Required. Builds the row for each item. If it does not return a component, the returned value is wrapped in one. The item arrives exactly as it was given in the data (see Data is used as given ). itemHeight number \| (item: T, index: number) => number Required. The pixel height of each item. A number: all rows are the same; a function: a known height per row (see Variable height ). pageSize number How many items to ask for in each request (50 by default). mainTemplate (content, state) => any The layout that wraps the list; see A custom container . loadingTemplate (state) => any The view shown while the first load is in progress. emptyTemplate () => any The view shown when there are no items left to show (the data is empty, or the filter removed all of them). errorTemplate (error) => any The view shown in place of the rows when the first load, refresh() or an automatic refresh request fails; if it is not given, the error is reported as MJX207 . An error in the next page request is always reported as MJX207 and written to getState().error ; the loaded rows stay on screen, the error view is not shown, the request is made again on the next scroll, and error is cleared on a successful load. filter (items: T[]) => T[] Applied to the loaded data; spacers and indices are calculated from the filtered length (see Filtering ). overscan number The number of extra rows drawn above and below the visible area (by default, the number of visible rows). cacheSize number The upper limit of row components kept in the cache, the drawn rows included (by default max(200, 3 × the number of drawn rows) ). When it is exceeded, the off-screen rows not seen for the longest time are disposed. autoRefresh boolean When the reactive data read inside dataRequest changes, it fetches the loaded range again in a single request (on by default); see Automatic refresh . With false , the list refreshes only with refresh() . watch () => unknown An extra dependency for automatic refresh: reactive fields read here trigger a reload too. autoLoad boolean Asks for the next page when nearing the bottom (on by default). The next page is also asked for when the drawn window comes within overscan of the end of the loaded data (e.g. when the first page does not fill the visible area). autoLoadThreshold number How many pixels before the bottom edge of the loaded data the next page is asked for (100 by default). With a fixed height, the bottom edge is data.length × itemHeight . className string A class added to the root div . style Partial<CSSStyleDeclaration> Inline style for the root div . It is applied after the list's own overflow-y , height and position values; if you give the same property, yours wins. overscanPages , renderMode , pageBuffer Reserved; they are not read.

title: Virtual Lists (Virtualization)
heading: The dataRequest contract
text: dataRequest receives a request object ( VirtualizationDataRequest ): Field Type Meaning page number The zero-based page number. pageSize number The number of items asked for. In an automatic refresh the loaded range is asked for in a single request, so page is 0 and pageSize is pageSize × the number of loaded pages . scrollTop number The scroll position at the time of the request (0 on the first load). and gives a Promise that returns a response object ( VirtualizationDataResponse<T> ): Field Type Meaning items T[] The items on this page. totalCount number The number of items in the whole data set. It is written to state.totalCount (e.g. for showing the total in a header) and decides the size of the scroll area while hasMore holds. hasMore boolean Whether there is a next page. When it returns false , automatic loading stops. The scroll area covers the whole totalCount : items that are not loaded yet take up space in the bottom spacer, at their full height with a fixed itemHeight , and at the average of the loaded rows with a height given as a function. When you scroll into the unloaded region, pages are asked for in order until they reach it. When hasMore becomes false , or totalCount is less than the loaded items, the area is calculated from the loaded data only. filter is applied to the loaded items; the unloaded part is counted unfiltered, and the area shrinks as the items the filter drops are loaded.

title: Virtual Lists (Virtualization)
heading: Automatic refresh — autoRefresh
text: autoRefresh (on by default) calls dataRequest inside an effect on the first load and on refresh() . When one of the reactive fields read in this call changes, the loaded range (from page 0 to the current page) is fetched again in a single request; the rows of items still found in the response are kept, and those of the missing ones are disposed (see The rendering model ). Next-page requests are not tracked; setData() stops the tracking. In the example, notes.list(folder, state.query) reads the notes array, the search text and the archive, pin and date fields of the notes (and the title and body too while the search is filled in); when one of them changes, the list refreshes. The compiler wraps the await s in an async dataRequest function written on the tag: reactive fields read after an await become dependencies too (elsewhere, reads after await are not tracked; see Reads after await ). If dataRequest is defined outside the tag, or a dependency comes from somewhere else, give an extra dependency with watch={() => state.query} . The compiler applies the await wrapping only to a dataRequest written on a <Virtualization> tag; without JSX, only the reactive fields read before the first await become dependencies (see Reads after await ). A dependency read after an await or coming from somewhere else is given with watch: () => state.query . watch is called once while tracking is being set up, inside the same effect as dataRequest ; the fields it reads are added to the dependencies, and an error it throws is reported as MJX205 . The reload happens on the microtask after the change; the content stays in place until the response arrives. If more than 30 reloads are triggered within a second (loop protection), tracking is stopped and an MJX206 warning is written in development mode; refresh() sets the tracking up again.

title: Virtual Lists (Virtualization)
heading: Templates and the list state
text: mainTemplate and loadingTemplate receive the list's state ( VirtualizationState<T> ). The state fields are reactive; a field read through a getter in a template stays up to date. The data field announces that the loaded array, or the array given with setData , has changed, but it does not wrap the items (see Data is used as given ). Field Type Meaning isLoading boolean The first load or a refresh() request is in progress. isInitialized boolean The first response has arrived, or setData() was called. currentPage number The last loaded page. totalCount number The totalCount from the last response. hasMore boolean The hasMore from the last response. error Error \| undefined The error of the last request; cleared on a successful load. data T[] The loaded items (with no filter applied), as they were given.

title: Virtual Lists (Virtualization)
heading: Data is used as given
text: The list does not turn the data into reactive objects. The items returned by dataRequest or given to setData reach itemTemplate , itemHeight and filter as they are; the very array given to setData is read as state.data and getState().data . Reactive data stays reactive, and plain data stays plain. A row built with a plain object does not show a value written to the object later on its own. If the row needs to follow the change, give the data with reactive ; with plain data, the change is brought to the screen by running the row's bindings again with setState() (see Where reactivity meets the DOM ). If a new array has arrived, call setData . Later pages are not appended to the first page's array: the list collects the loaded items in its own array, and the arrays returned by dataRequest do not change.

title: Virtual Lists (Virtualization)
heading: A custom container — mainTemplate
text: mainTemplate builds the layout that wraps the list. Its first parameter ( content ) is the component that carries the rows; wherever it is put in the layout, the rows are drawn there. The nearest element wrapping it becomes the scroll container: the list gives it overflow-y: auto; position: relative; overflow-anchor: none and listens to its scrolling, while you give its height. In this case no style is written on the root div . A list with a header that shows the folder name and the total number of notes: The <content></content> tag places the content parameter. content is a component, so it is added to the scroll container's controls . mainTemplate is called once, in the list's constructor; the first request is made when content starts being built.

title: Virtual Lists (Virtualization)
heading: Filtering
text: The list can be filtered in two places: Inside dataRequest . The search in the example works this way: notes.list(folder, state.query) returns only the matching notes, and totalCount and hasMore are calculated from the filtered data. If the filter reads a reactive field, automatic refresh updates the list on its own. With the filter prop. The function is applied to all the loaded data on every load (first load, next page, refresh, setData ); spacers, indices and itemHeight totals are calculated from the filtered list, and state.data stays unfiltered. Since the filter runs only on loading, if a field it reads changes later, the list does not refresh on its own; call refresh() or move the condition into dataRequest . If the filter removes all the loaded items, emptyTemplate is shown, and if it is not given, the list area stays empty; the next page is not asked for, even if there are more pages on the server. If matching items can be on later pages, do the filtering in dataRequest .

title: Virtual Lists (Virtualization)
heading: Variable height and size changes
text: If the rows have different heights that can be calculated in advance, give itemHeight a function; for example (note) => (note.body ? 72 : 48) if the row of a note with a body is taller. The heights are summed once every time the data changes (a load, setData , filter ); the visible range is found with a binary search, and scrollToIndex uses these totals as well. Invalid values ( NaN , negative) count as 0. The list does not track heights: even if the value itemHeight reads is reactive, it does not notice the change on its own. When the data stays the same but the height of one or more rows changes (a row expanded, the density setting changed, a fixed itemHeight number was replaced with another number), call updateHeights() . The method reads the heights again from scratch and redraws the window; the rows stay as they are, filter does not run again, and no load is requested. The row at the top of the screen keeps its place on screen, as on a data change : if a row above it grows, the scroll position shifts by the same amount. If a height can only be known by measuring after drawing (a feed of free-form text), this method is not suitable. When the size of the list's container changes (a screen rotation, the mobile keyboard opening, the window size), the visible rows are recalculated without waiting for a scroll. A ResizeObserver is used for this; if the environment does not have one, this step is skipped, and the observer is released when the list is disposed.

title: Virtual Lists (Virtualization)
heading: The rendering model and methods
text: Only a window of rows is in the DOM: [anchor − overscan, anchor + visible + overscan) , anchor = floor(scrollTop / itemHeight) . The rows are plain siblings between two spacer div s; the spacer heights are never negative, and top + rows + bottom = filtered length × itemHeight . A row that leaves the window is not disposed but detached from the DOM ; when it comes back, the same component (its bindings, input state, item object) is put back at its ordered position. No placeholder comments pile up. A detached row gets onDeactivated , and a row put back gets onActivated . When cacheSize is exceeded, the rows not seen for the longest time are disposed. Rows are cached by the identity of the item object (by position for primitive items). The same object can appear in the data more than once; each occurrence gets its own row. setData , automatic refresh and the arrival of the next page match the rows by this identity: the row of an object still found in the new view is kept, whether it is on screen or in the cache, and moved to its new position; the row of an object not found in the new view (including those the filter drops along with the next page) is disposed. An object finds the same row whether it is given in raw form or as its reactive proxy. For a primitive item, the same value at the same position keeps its row. If new objects arrive on every load (e.g. a fresh list from the server), the rows are rebuilt even if they carry the same id . The index a kept row received from itemTemplate is its position at the moment it was built; it is not updated afterwards. When the data changes ( setData , automatic refresh, the next page), the first of the rows visible on screen that stays in the new data keeps its place on screen: if items are added above it or deleted from above it (also when the next page's items move above it through a sorting filter ), the scroll position shifts by that much, and when the order changes, the scroll follows that row to its new place. For a primitive item, the same value is looked for at the position closest to its old one. If none of the visible rows remains, the drawn row closest to the screen is used, first among those above the screen and then among those below it; if none of them remains either, the scroll position is kept as it is. If a row that overflows the top of the screen gets shorter, part of it stays visible. While the list is at the very top, it stays at the top, and an item added at the top is visible. To go back to the start of the list after a new sort, call scrollToIndex(0) . The position is read from the rows drawn on screen, so it stays correct even if the array is changed in place ( splice , sort ) and the same array is given again. The scroll container is given overflow-anchor: none : the list keeps the position, not the browser; the browser's own scroll anchoring could change the scroll position while the list is drawing rows and leave a gap in the visible area. The window is recalculated on every scroll event (also while hasMore is false ); only the difference between the old and the new window is processed. The first request is made while the list is being built; a list held with x-wait is not built, so its first request is also postponed until the wait ends. The first draw waits for layout: if the scroll container is not in document yet, drawing is postponed to onMounted ; for a container that is in the document but has a height of 0, drawing happens when the container's size changes. Method Effect refresh() Resets the data and asks for page 0 again with dataRequest ; all rows in the cache are disposed. Sets up automatic refresh tracking again. Returns a Promise . setData(items) Changes the data without making a request; hasMore becomes false , the page becomes 0, and automatic refresh stops. The rows of items still found in the new data are kept, and those of the missing ones are disposed. updateHeights() When the data stays the same but heights change, reads the heights again and draws the window; the rows are kept, and the row at the top of the screen stays in place (see Variable height ). scrollToIndex(i) Scrolls to the position of row i ( i × itemHeight with a fixed height) and draws right away; an index out of range is clamped to the edge. getState() A shallow copy of the list state. The methods are on the list component itself; in JSX you reach it through ref (see Element access inside a component ). The methods are called on the component built with new Virtualization(...) .

title: Virtual Lists (Virtualization)
heading: When to use it?
text: Situation Recommendation Few items (< ~100), variable height The normal list binding ( Conditional Rendering and Lists ). Many items, a fixed or precomputable row height Virtualization ( itemHeight as a number or a function). Infinite scrolling / a paged API Virtualization + autoLoad .

heading: Next step
